roles.heroLead: A builder-grade shower was built to survive the walkthrough — not twenty Ridge winters. Since tile and grout merely shed water, the bonded membrane behind them does the stopping. We assemble that hidden system correctly, hold a flood test for a full 24 hours, photograph it, and set tile only afterward.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Snoqualmie, WA?
roles.costP1: Snoqualmie tile work starts near $14 and reaches $26 per square foot installed — labor, tile, substrate prep and setting materials combined — and labor's own line starts at $11/sq ft. Tub-shower surrounds commonly quote $3,200–$6,800; a full bathroom of shower, floor and niche spans $6,500 through $14,000; a lone bathroom floor, call it 45 sq ft, runs $900–$1,600.
roles.costP2: What moves the bid isn't the tile's price tag — it's the format. Trendy mosaic sheets at $4 can out-cost a $12 large-format plank once installed, since every extra cut and grout line is labor, and labor is most of what you're paying for.
roles.costNote: Snoqualmie-area installed ranges, current August 2026, covering tile, materials and labor. Your written on-site quote is the number to trust.
roles.layersLead: Count them: seven layers under and behind your tile. The failed showers we open are missing one — the membrane, nearly every time — because somebody saved a few hundred dollars on build day and left the next owner a five-figure teardown.
roles.whyP1: A shortcut shower fails on a schedule: water slips past grout, sits in the substrate, and announces itself years later — a soft hallway floor, a stain blooming on the ceiling below — often just after the builder's warranty runs out. By then you're rebuilding framing, subfloor and drywall before any new tile.
roles.whyP2: About a tenth of shower cost is waterproofing. That's the line a builder trims to save hundreds — and the owner later covers in tens of thousands.
roles.scopeIntro: Treat these as opening figures — layout complexity, substrate condition and format all shift them. Your binding number is written on site, at no charge.
roles.cardShower: In sequence: pre-sloped base, bonded membrane, flood test with photos, then niche and curb — or curbless entry — with tile last. The half you'll never see is the half doing the work.
roles.cardFloors: Bathrooms, kitchens, mudrooms, entries and basements — subfloor brought flat first, with an uncoupling membrane wherever radiant heat or movement asks for it.
roles.cardBacksplash: Slab-look porcelain, herringbone, subway or mosaic sheet. Outlets cut clean, edges trimmed, grout keyed to the countertop instead of whatever came in the box.
roles.cardHeated: Radiant mat on an uncoupling membrane, resistance-checked before setting and again after, running on a dedicated circuit. Worth doing only while the floor's already open.
roles.cardRepair: Cracked field tile, failing grout, shower corners letting go. You'll get a straight answer on whether it's fixable or the substrate underneath is done.
roles.cardDemo: Old surround, thinset and backer board out — dust boxed in behind plastic and negative air, debris hauled the same day. The driveway stays yours.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Snoqualmie, WA?
roles.faqA1: Between $14 and $26 for the installed square foot is the honest total for Snoqualmie tile — labor, tile, setting materials and substrate prep all in — and you can count $11 per square foot as labor's opening rate. Typical jobs: a tub-shower surround asks $3,200 to $6,800; a 45-square-foot bathroom floor sits near $900–$1,600; a complete bathroom of floor, shower and niche comes to $6,500–$14,000. Format swings the bill harder than tile price — mosaics and large planks both devour labor a 12×12 never asks for.
roles.faqQ2: How much does a tiled shower cost in Snoqualmie?
roles.faqA2: Standard alcove showers here budget in the $3,200–$6,800 band. Covered inside: removal of the old surround, a pre-sloped pan with the waterproofing bonded over it, setting, niche and grout. Steam, benches, curbless entries and stone to the ceiling all land above the band. Call waterproofing ten percent of the invoice — the ten percent that stands between you and a framing repair with five figures on it.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Every single time — this step is why people hire us. The build: base pre-sloped, an ANSI A118.10 membrane bonded and carried wall-high to TCNA methods, every corner, seam and penetration closed off, and 24 hours of flood testing photographed before tile goes anywhere. Tile isn't waterproof and neither is grout; the membrane behind them is what defends the framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Four to six working days is standard for a Snoqualmie bathroom: demo and dust walls on day one, substrate plus waterproofing on day two with the flood test running 24 hours behind it, tile setting for a day or two, then grout, silicone and trim to finish. Keep the shower dry another 24 hours while grout cures. A floor on its own usually takes one or two days.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain belongs wherever water or wear shows up — floors, showers, hard-working rooms — thanks to its tighter body: sub-0.5% absorption and real chip resistance. For wall duty and backsplash work, budget-friendly ceramic does the job happily. The Snoqualmie spec we default to: porcelain across each floor and shower pan; glass or ceramic wherever the assignment is purely visual.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes. Fog on the Ridge makes a warm floor feel less like luxury and more like sense. Electric radiant prices at $11–$16 the square foot installed, thermostat within, over an uncoupling membrane, resistance-tested ahead of tiling and again once it's down, on its own circuit. Adding it is only economical while the floor is up — so make the call before the remodel starts, not afterward.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Nearly every time. From $3.50 a square foot for removal with haul-away, demo buys the single opportunity to check the subfloor for movement or concealed water damage — exactly what a twenty-year-old builder install tends to hide — and to hold the new floor to the right height at doorways. Yes, tile can go over flat, sound, well-bonded tile, but doing so buries problems we would rather meet early.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Snoqualmie?
roles.faqA8: In Snoqualmie a standard 30 sq ft kitchen backsplash runs $1,100–$2,200 installed, with outlet holes cut, edges trimmed and grout tuned to the counter. Layout drives where you land in that range: herringbone, mosaic sheets, picture-frame details behind the range and full-height slab-look porcelain all add cutting and layout time.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Frequently. Repairs and regrouting start at $8 per square foot — the move when grout has stained or started crumbling, when an impact cracked a tile or two, or when shower corners need old grout swapped for silicone. The wrong call is patching over a failed substrate: hollow-sounding tile, pieces loosening in a pattern, a wall with any give. That buys months, not years — and we'll tell you which situation you have before quoting.
roles.faqQ10: Which Snoqualmie neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: Everywhere in town — Snoqualmie Ridge, downtown Snoqualmie, Kimball Creek and Meadowbrook — plus the Valley around it: Fall City, North Bend, Preston, Carnation, Si View, Tanner, Riverbend, Wilderness Rim, Lake Alice and up to Snoqualmie Pass. Mirrormont, the Issaquah Highlands and the rest of the Eastside are an easy run too.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Two full years of workmanship warranty come with OC Flooring tile — intentionally beyond our carpet term, because tile shows its problems in the second year, hardly ever the second week. A manufacturer's complete waterproofing assembly brings its own system warranty alongside. And since membrane and flood test are photographed every time, proof of what sits behind your tile genuinely exists — more than most builder paperwork can claim.
